# Bluestone

**[Download bluestone-a67lg2.zip](https://github.com/CyberspaceVii/bluestone-a67lg2/releases/download/v0.4/bluestone-a67lg2.zip)**

Blocks the factory Rsota updater and Google Play services' firmware-installation
path on the **Foxxd A67L Gen 2**. Shows an ongoing notification and retains
available update offers for inspection. A WebUI provides status and export.

**v0.4 beta — Android 16 / KernelSU Next / SELinux Enforcing.** The
[Gen 1 module](https://github.com/CyberspaceVii/bluestone-a67lg1) remains separate;
these changes have not been validated on Gen 1.

## What happens when an update is offered

Google firmware-updater calls are denied before dispatch to the native updater.
When Play services exposes an offer in its local updater preferences, Bluestone
saves its URL and metadata privately and alerts you. It attempts to save a
separate inspection copy over **validated, unmetered Wi-Fi**.

Open **KernelSU Next → Modules → Bluestone → WebUI** to see protection status
and retained offers. **Export for inspection** writes an inspection ZIP into
**Downloads/Bluestone**. That bundle contains the offer metadata, a status
record and the firmware package when a complete copy was saved. An incomplete
transfer is explicitly named `package.zip.part`.

The module has **no install, proceed, resume or reboot action**. A saved package
is not a promise that installation is safe, compatible or will preserve root.
Hashes identify retained bytes; firmware signatures are not verified by this
module. The exported inspection bundle is not an installable KernelSU module.

## Storage and notifications

- Private cache: `/data/adb/bluestone/updates/`. No automatic deletion of older
  offers, packages or existing backups. At most 64 offer records are retained;
  manage old records with a root file manager if that limit is reached.
- At most 512 MiB per package and 1 GiB total cache, keeping 1 GiB free in
  reserve. Oversized packages and storage failures leave metadata and an
  explicit status; the firmware block stays active.
- Only recognized Google HTTPS OTA URLs are downloaded. Unsupported URLs or
  redirects remain metadata-only/save-failed records, never fake saved packages.
- Previously saved copies are reused. Interrupted downloads remain partial;
  **Retry saving package** explicitly replaces that offer's incomplete copy.
- Export makes another copy and also keeps the free-space reserve. It uses
  unique filenames, refuses symlink paths and never overwrites an existing file.
- Repeated observations of the same offer are deduplicated. The ongoing
  notification is refreshed daily; dismissing or muting it does not unblock OTA.
  Notifications are posted through Android System with the title **Bluestone**.

## Install

1. Finish any existing OTA or snapshot merge first. The installer requires an
   idle updater and clean snapshot state; it does not cancel or reset either.
2. Download the [latest ZIP](https://github.com/CyberspaceVii/bluestone-a67lg2/releases/latest/download/bluestone-a67lg2.zip).
3. In KernelSU Next, install the ZIP from storage and reboot when you choose.
4. Open Bluestone's WebUI and check that protection is active. Installation
   alone does not establish that the boot-time rule has taken effect.

Requirements: `ro.product.device=A67L_Gen2`, Android 16 API 36, KernelSU Next
with deny-rule support, Google Play services and SELinux Enforcing. No Zygisk
or Xposed dependency. The existing systemless Rsota removal is retained.

## Scope and limitations

The policy removes the `gmscore_app → update_engine` Binder **call** permission.
It does not stop Play services, disable all Google networking, stop the native
updater, or change the updater's permissions. Ordinary app updates and
Mainline/Google Play system updates are outside this policy. Representative
system-server/APEX Binder permissions were verified unchanged; an actual app
or Mainline update installation was not performed during validation.

Offer discovery depends on the observed Play services preference format and a
15-second observation interval. An offer never written there, or removed before
observation, may not be archived. The permission block operates independently
of observation, notifications and download success.
Offer collection and exports currently target the owner profile (user 0).

This covers the observed Google firmware client and Rsota, not every possible
privileged updater. Root tools, other SELinux domains and future policy/client
changes require separate assessment. A WebUI warning means protection could
not be established; it must not be treated as a successful block.

## Disable or uninstall

Disable/remove Bluestone in KernelSU Next and reboot to restore the normal
boot-time policy and Rsota. Existing deny rules remain in the running policy
until reboot; disabling the module is not an immediate permission restoration.
Retained files in `/data/adb/bluestone/` and exported bundles remain for you to
manage. No update is automatically resumed or installed.

## Build and validation

Source and build script are included. With Android SDK platform 37, build-tools
37.0.0 and NDK 30.0.16248370 installed:

```sh
python3 build.py --output /tmp/bluestone-a67lg2.zip
```

Set `BLUESTONE_ANDROID_SDK` / `BLUESTONE_ANDROID_NDK` for other installation
paths. See [validation](VALIDATION.md) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).
